A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PERM and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. Text and visual comparison support a reliable assessment of the complete work.

before.justification: v5 reports original reconstruction experiments in Tables 1–3, architecture ablations, baseline comparisons, and qualitative synthesis, reconstruction, and editing results.

after.justification: v6 retains these original quantitative experiments, ablations, and qualitative application results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The frequency-domain PCA representation, guide/residual decomposition, network components, losses, and inference procedures are unchanged. The GroomGen revisions concern attribution and interpretation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same augmented USC-HairSalon data, 17 public evaluation hairstyles, private 80-hairstyle dataset, and application scenarios. Describing Figure 25 as long kinky hair does not introduce a different test input.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets and official-checkpoint comparisons are unchanged. Figures 7 and 27 now explicitly identify the authors' GroomGen implementation, which v5 already disclosed in Section 4.2 and Appendix B.6.

E3.justification: Data splits, metrics, model sizes, training budgets, and testing procedures remain unchanged. Figure 25 retains the same 200-point original strands, downsampling to 100 points, and latent-code reconstruction; the explanation of that resolution choice changes.

E4.justification: The component ablations, PCA sensitivity analyses, checkpoint checks, and strand-resolution experiment remain unchanged. Figure 25 drops the motivating GroomGen teaser illustration but retains the same diagnostic test and its outputs.

E5.justification: Run and seed reporting practices are unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the reported numerical comparisons are unchanged. Section 4.2 retains position/curvature errors of 1.658/0.769 for PERM and 2.570/6.199 for the GroomGen implementation. Experimental output images are retained; the removed Figure 25 panel is an external teaser reference.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, PCA decomposition, losses, optimization objectives, and metric definitions are unchanged, including Equations 1–9. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: disentangled control of global hair structure and local curls, a compact parametric representation, and reuse across hair-related applications.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 narrows the 100-point limitation from kinky hairstyles generally to long kinky hairstyles. Appendix C.4 attributes reconstruction failure to 'our implementation' instead of 'the architecture' and describes downsampling as fitting the authors' design. Appendix E's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware/software, training times, and resource-access information are unchanged. The GroomGen reimplementation and its 100-point representation were already documented in v5; the revised attribution adds no new setting.

R1.justification: Appendix C.4 removes the explicit connection to GroomGen's teaser and the statement attributing the 100-point requirement to its published architecture, narrowing that criticism to the authors' implementation. The bibliography and main related-work section remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting is localized to the GroomGen discussion in Section 4.2 and Appendix C.4, with a small abstract wording adjustment and paragraph reflow. The document's section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 25 changes from four panels to three by removing the GroomGen reference and enlarging the retained images. Captions for Figures 7, 25, and 27 explicitly identify the authors' implementation. Subsequent appendix text and figures undergo limited layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v6 improves attribution and qualification of the GroomGen comparison: revised captions identify reimplementation results, and Section 4.2 and Appendix C.4 narrow the failure interpretation. The gain is limited because the experiments are unchanged, removing the teaser reduces visual context, and Section 2 still retains broader criticism of GroomGen.
